questions.stem: A 58-year-old patient is diagnosed with ovarian cancer and was started on cisplatin but complains of severe vomiting after 6 hrs of starting cisplatin. Which of the following medications would be most effective to counteract the emesis in this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ondansetron
  • 5HT3 antagonists like Ondansetron are the drug of choice for the early phase( < 24hr) of Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
  • NK 1 Antagonist is the drug of choice for the delayed phase of Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 717

questions.stem: The Anti-emetic activity of metoclopramide is mainly because of:
questions.solutionHtml:
D2 antagonism
  • Metoclopramide:

    • Metoclopramide has Antiemetic & Prokinetic properties. Its antiemetic property is due to D2 antagonism, and 5HT3 antagonism(seen at a higher dose) and its Prokinetic action is due to 5HT4 agonism. Prokinetic action is by increasing lower esophageal sphincter tone, and small intestinal contractions and stimulating GIT motility but no effect on large intestine motility


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 713

questions.stem: Which of the following is false about action of metoclopropamide on digestive tract?

options.label: C
options.text: Has clinically significant effects on large-bowel motility

questions.answerText: Has clinically significant effects on large-bowel motility
questions.solutionHtml:
Has clinically significant effects on large-bowel motility
  • Action of metoclopropamide on digestive tract
  • Effects are confined largely to the upper digestive tract
  • It increases lower esophageal sphincter tone and stimulates antral and small intestinal contractions.
  • It has no clinically significant effects on large-bowel motility


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 923

questions.stem: A 2-year-old child with protracted vomiting was given an anti-emetic and he develops abnormal posturing. Which drug was given?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metoclopramide
  • It causes D2 blockade in CNS
  • Extrapyramidal Effects (due to D2 blockade in CNS)
  • Restlessness, Akathesia, drug-induced Parkinsonism
  • So the Causative Agent Is Metoclopropamide


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 713

questions.stem: A patient was given an antiemetic metoclopramide by IV Injection for vomiting. He developed dystonia after taking it. What is given for the treatment of dystonia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Benztropine
  • The major side effects of metoclopramide include extrapyramidal effects.
  • Dystonia, usually occurs acutely after intravenous administration
  • Dystonia will respond to treatment with anticholinergic (trihexyphenidyl (benzhexol), benztropine, and biperiden) or antihistaminic drugs


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 923

questions.stem: 5HT3 Antagonist approved for delayed CINV (Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting) is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Palonosetron
  • Palonosetron injection is used to prevent nausea and vomiting that is caused by cancer medicines (chemotherapy).
  • It is also used to prevent nausea and vomiting that may occur after surgery. Palonosetron works by blocking the signals to the brain that cause nausea and vomiting.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 717

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about Hyoscine:

options.label: C
options.text: Can be used in post-operative vomiting

options.label: D
options.text: Most effective drug for motion sickness

questions.answerText: Can be used in post-operative vomiting
questions.solutionHtml:
Can be used in post-operative vomiting
  • Hyoscine:
  • Is the most effective drug for motion sickness
  • It has a brief duration of action when used as a tablet.
  • Due to anticholinergic property produces sedation, dry mouth, and other anticholinergic side effects; suitable only for short brisk journies
  • Antiemetic mechanism of action:
  • Action is exerted probably by blocking conduction of nerve impulses across a cholinergic link in the pathway leading from the vestibular apparatus to the vomiting center and has poor efficacy in vomiting of other etiologies.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi,7th Edition Page Number: 663

questions.stem: A drug that acts by inhibiting the influx of Ca2+ from endolymph into the vestibular sensory cells is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cinnarizine
  • It blocks the effects of histamine in your brain to reduce symptoms of travel sickness. It also acts as a calcium channel blocker.
  • This helps improve blood flow in the inner ear and reduces symptoms caused by vertigo, tinnitus, and Ménière's disease.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 712

questions.stem: A 29-year-old male with testicular cancer is receiving cisplatin-based chemotherapy. He has been given dexamethasone, metoclopramide, and aprepitant prior to receiving chemotherapy. He is now agitated, very anxious, and complaining of abnormal eye movements. What is the best immediate treatment?
questions.solutionHtml:
Benztropine
  • The patient is having Occulo lyric crisis due to metoclopramide
  • The major side effects of metoclopramide include extrapyramidal effects like dystonia, Occulo lyric crisis
  • Dystonia, usually occur acutely after intravenous administration
  • Dystonia’s will respond to treatment with anticholinergic (trihexyphenidyl (benzhexol), benztropine and biperiden) or antihistaminic drugs


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 923

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his brother after trying to jump out of a moving car. He says that the state police have been following him for the last 7 months. He recently quit his job at a local consulting firm to work on his mission to rid the world of evil. He does not smoke, drink alcoholic beverages, or use illicit drugs. He takes no medications. His temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), pulse is 90/min, respirations are 20/min, and blood pressure is 120/86 mm Hg. On mental status examination, his response to the first question lasted 5 minutes without interruption. He switched topics a number of times and his speech was pressured. He spoke excessively about his plan to "bring absolute justice to the world". He has a labile effect. There is no evidence of suicidal ideation. A toxicology screen is negative. He is admitted to the hospital for his symptoms and starts therapy. One week later, he develops difficulty walking and a tremor that improves with activity. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's latest symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dopamine antagonist.
  • This patient's combination of delusions for at least 6 months, as well as his pressured and disorganized speech indicates schizophrenia. His current difficulty walking and tremor following treatment suggest that he has developed extrapyramidal symptoms.

  • Dopamine 2 receptor antagonism is the main mechanism of action for antipsychotics, especially first-generation antipsychotics such as haloperidol. All antipsychotics that interact with the D2 receptor can cause extrapyramidal syndrome, but this effect is particularly pronounced in the use of first-generation antipsychotics due to their high affinity to D2 receptors.

  • Patients who have taken antipsychotics on the scale of days to weeks can show parkinsonism, including tremors, rigidity, and shuffling gait, which the patient in the vignette has. Management of EPS symptoms can be treated with an anticholinergic (e.g., benztropine), a dopamine agonist (e.g., amantadine), and reducing or omitting the offending drug.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:467.

questions.stem: A previously healthy 5-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department because of difficulty breathing and vomiting that began 1 hour after she took an amoxicillin tablet. She appears anxious. Her pulse is 140/min, respirations are 40/min, and her blood pressure is 72/39 mmHg. She has several well-circumscribed, raised, erythematous plaques scattered diffusely over her trunk and extremities. Pulmonary examination shows diffuse, bilateral wheezing. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Epinephrine
  • The patient's acute hypotension, tachycardia, respiratory distress, and dermatologic findings in the setting of recent antibiotic use are consistent with anaphylaxis.
  • Epinephrine should be administered immediately if anaphylaxis, a type I hypersensitivity reaction, is suspected. Epinephrine acts at both beta-adrenergic receptors (at lower doses) and alpha-adrenergic receptors (at higher doses) to help increase blood pressure, increase bronchodilation, reduce mucosal edema in the upper airway, and reduce the release of inflammatory mediators from mast cells and basophils.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:467.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with gastroesophageal reflux disease comes to the physician because of severe burning chest pain and belching after meals. He has limited his caffeine intake and has been avoiding food close to bedtime. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy shows erythema and erosions in the distal esophagus. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of the most appropriate drug for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibition of H+K+ ATPase.
  • This patient has symptoms consistent with severe GERD, and evidence of reflux-induced esophagitis. A proton pump inhibitor (PPI) would be the appropriate first-line drug therapy for this patient.

  • Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) irreversibly inhibit H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells of the stomach and thus reduce the ATP-dependent secretion of H+ ions into the gastric lumen. They are considered first-line for patients with severe GERD.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:700.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with a history of myocardial infarction is admitted to the hospital for treatment of atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. He is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 80 kg (173 lb). He is given an intravenous bolus of 150 mg of amiodarone. After 20 minutes, the amiodarone plasma concentration is 2.5 ?g/mL. Amiodarone distributes in the body within minutes, and its elimination half-life after intravenous administration is 30 days. Which of the following values is closest to the volume of distribution of the administered drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
60L

The volume of distribution is the theoretical volume that would contain the total amount of the drug within the body at a concentration equal to that present in plasma.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:577,578.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an adverse effect of Cimetidine?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hepatic failure
  • Cimetidine Adverse Effects: Headache, dizziness, bowel upset, dry mouth, rashes
  • Has antiandrogenic action displaces dihydrotestosterone from its cytoplasmic receptor
  • increases plasma prolactin and inhibits degradation of estradiol by liver
  • High doses given for long periods have produced gynecomastia, loss of libido, impotence and a temporary decrease in sperm count, galactorrhoea
  • Transient elevation of plasma aminotransferases; but hepatotoxicity is rare.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 698

questions.stem: We have two patients. One requires suppression of emesis caused by an anticancer drug that causes a high incidence and severity of vomiting (highly emetogenic drug). Another patient has severe diabetic gastroparesis and gastroesophageal reflux, which requires relief. Which one drug would be suitable for both indications (assuming no specific contraindications)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metoclopramide
  • Metoclopramide has clinically useful antiemetic and prokinetic actions and would be suitable for either of the patients described in the question.
  • The antiemetic effect arises from the blockade of dopamine (and, probably, serotonin) receptors in the brain’s chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ).
  • The drug is indicated for not only chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, but also that which may occur with radiation therapy, postoperatively, or in response to opioid analgesics or emetogenic toxins.
  • The enhanced gastric and upper intestinal motility probably reflects an enhancement of the expected effects of ACh on muscarinic receptors found on the longitudinal smooth muscle in the GI tract.
  • Metoclopramide raises the lower oesophageal sphincter tone and relaxes the pyloric sphincter, which hastens gastric emptying.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 713
